messages.subject: two x-axis graph
parts:
Hello group, I was looking through the gallery and cannot find a good template for trying to model something rather simple. What I want to do is take some users in two generic groups (1 and 2), list them down the side of a graph with two x-axes (group 1 on X1, group 2 on X2) with no y-axis, and then draw a line between a member of group 1 and group 2 when the user indicates they are connected.

output could look like this, but graphical.
Group 1 Group 2
A            9
B            6
C            7
D            5
E           11
F            2
G           4

For example, if the user indicated that there was an association between C and 4, imagine a line is drawn between Group 1 (C) and Group 2 (4). I know how I would model the data inputting* but don't know how to draw the graphical representation. I wanted it to update in real time so I chose Shiny but maybe python is better for this (or I may need to dust off my java.awt.* ... oh noes!! ....)

thx!
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] two x-axis graph
parts:
Hi Chris, 
This sounds like more of a visualization question for R in general and not related to shinyapps.io.  I am afraid I don't have any great suggestions for you since I have never had such a use case.  Maybe you could use something like Diagrammer, check out some examples here: http://www.htmlwidgets.org/showcase_diagrammer.html

If not, maybe folks on StackOverflow could point you to something a bit more to your liking.
-Tareef
